R12, and it is RIGHT — I declared `self` first and the guard corrected me. The diff touches scripts/ops/session_registry.py, which is landing machinery: it mints the spawn prompt that tells every child how to declare a tier, arm auto-merge and claim the R13 merge slot. R12's reasoning applies even though my edit there is SIX LINES and prints an advisory to stderr — 'a PR that edits the rules by which PRs land must not be merged by those rules unread', and the guard grades the DIFF rather than my account of it, which is the property that makes it worth having. The tier is not the objection and R12 says so.

WHAT A HUMAN IS BEING ASKED TO READ, in one line: the six-line block in cmd_register that prints `verdict['advisory']` to stderr when spawn_gate reports the named work object is not on the base ref. It changes no verdict, no return code and no written row — the spawn VERDICT is byte-for-byte what it was, pinned by controls in both directions (a branch-only in-priority spawn still PERMITS; an on-base out-of-priority spawn is still REFUSED). Everything else in the diff is scripts/ops/spawn_gate.py and the backlog row.

I considered splitting the print into its own PR so the rest could self-land, and did NOT, because it would ship an advisory that is computed and discarded — the written-and-never-read defect this repo has a guard for — for however long the second PR sat.
why:
Closes BL-20260907-DISPATCH-NAMES-A-WORK-OBJECT-THAT-WAS-NEVER-CREATED. Tier-1: scripts/ops/** and docs/claude/**. No src/, no config, no order path; the spawn VERDICT is byte-for-byte unchanged.

⚠️ HALF OF WHAT THIS ROW ASKS FOR ALREADY EXISTED AND I NEARLY SHIPPED A SECOND COPY. I wrote a work-object existence check into session_registry.register, and only on exercising the real cmd_register found that scripts/ops/spawn_gate.py::grade already REFUSES an object that 'names no file under docs/claude/work/objects/'. That is RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED, the recurrence ledger's own class; the duplicate was REVERTED before anything landed (git checkout, session_registry --self-test PASS) and is recorded rather than quietly dropped. The cheap existence check CLAUDE.md prescribes is what caught it, for the second time in this session.

WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING IS NARROWER THAN THE ROW'S TITLE, AND IS PRECISELY WHAT THE ROW MEASURED. spawn_gate reads the LOCAL filesystem, while the defect is that MI-156's object 'DID NOT EXIST on origin/main 383a4f7'. Different facts, and the difference IS the defect: a manager that authors the object in its own branch and spawns from that checkout passes the local check, while the child — which reads the base ref — finds nothing and transcribes its done_condition from the prompt, the exact failure the durable carrier exists to prevent.

SHIPPED IN THE SINGLE OWNER RATHER THAN BESIDE IT: spawn_gate grades base visibility in FOUR never-collapsed states — on_base / branch_only / base_unreadable (*we could not look*, never folded into on_base) / not_checked — and attaches an `advisory`.

⚠️ IT WARNS RATHER THAN REFUSING, DELIBERATELY. Authoring the object in the branch you spawn from is LEGITIMATE and common — MI-148's own note reads 'this branch creates it' — so refusing would break the correct flow to catch the incorrect one, and the row's criterion allows either ('REFUSES (or loudly warns on)'). What must not happen is silence. ⚠️ VISIBILITY CAN NEVER CHANGE THE VERDICT, pinned by controls in both directions (a branch-only in-priority spawn still PERMITS; an on-base out-of-priority spawn is still REFUSED). ⚠️ AND THE ADVISORY IS PRINTED, NOT MERELY COMPUTED — session_registry's spawn-gate site emits it to stderr, because a signal computed and discarded is worse than a missing one.

⚠️ A FAILED `git cat-file` IS NOT PROOF OF ABSENCE — it also fails when the base ref does not exist (a fresh clone, a detached CI checkout) — so object_on_base verifies the ref is READABLE before reading its silence as a fact. That is what keeps base_unreadable out of branch_only.

THE OBSERVATION THE CRITERION DEMANDS, through the REAL cmd_register with only REGISTRY_PATH redirected to a temp copy of SESSIONS.json (231 rows) so the shared register was never mutated — THREE ways, because a refusal without a pass proves only that the gate is a wall: (1) PLANTED NEGATIVE WO-99999999-THIS-OBJECT-DOES-NOT-EXIST -> spawn-gate [REFUSED], rc=3, rows 231 -> 231, nothing written. (2) PLANTED BRANCH-ONLY (authored on disk with the cycle's parent_intent, confirmed absent from origin/main) -> spawn-gate ⚠️ [BRANCH_ONLY] on stderr naming the consequence, rc=0, rows 231 -> 232, permitted. (3) POSITIVE CONTROL WO-20260903-AVAX-VENUE-MAX-OWN-THE-ORDER-PATH (on origin/main, parent_intent = the cycle's IN-20260903-TRADING-SYSTEM-HEALTH) -> rc=0, row written, NO advisory and NO refusal. Plus 9 planted controls in spawn_gate --self-test, all passing, and the pre-existing 30+ controls unchanged.

⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN CAVEATS ARE MET: 'a green registration is NOT the observation' — the planted negative and the planted branch-only are deliberate failures observed FIRING, not a quiet green; and 'fixing the two known instances by hand closes nothing' — neither was touched.
